text:
A study of sediment from Ostrava Lake, released on 14 March 2031, comes from the Sarnow Institute, whose researchers have documented a continuous record reaching back roughly 11,000 years.

Dr. Helena Voráčková, lead sedimentologist at the institute, presented the results. Core samples showed 4.2 meters of continuous sediment layers, she said, an unbroken sequence covering the Holocene.

The findings rest on the peer-reviewed paper "Holocene Sediment Sequences of Ostrava Lake," published in the *Sarnow Institute Quarterly Review of Earth Sciences*. The figures reported here are drawn from that paper and from Dr. Voráčková's presentation of it.

The institute's release identifies the paper as the basis for the study's conclusions.
